title: How targets are estimated
lead: Your targets start from one number, your bodyweight. Everything here is an estimate, and you can overwrite any of it in Nutrition targets.

steps.heading: Energy
steps.body: Bodyweight in kilograms × {kcalPerKgMaintenance} kcal, rounded to the nearest {energyKcalRoundTo}. It's a maintenance estimate for someone who trains a few days a week. It's never a deficit and never a surplus.

steps.heading: Protein
steps.body: Bodyweight in kilograms × {proteinGramsPerKg} g. Protein is set first, and the other two fit around it.

steps.heading: Fat
steps.body: {fatFloorPercentOfEnergy}% of the energy estimate, and never less than {fatFloorGramsPerKg} g per kilogram of bodyweight.

steps.heading: Carbs
steps.body: The energy left after protein and fat, never below zero.

steps.heading: Calories
steps.body: Counted from grams: {kcalPerGramProtein} kcal per gram of protein, {kcalPerGramCarbs} per gram of carbs, {kcalPerGramFat} per gram of fat. Today's calorie line adds up your three gram targets this way, so it can sit a little off the energy estimate.

steps.heading: Rounding
steps.body: Grams round to the nearest {macroGramsRoundTo}, so an estimate never reads like a measurement.

clinician: These are estimates and rules of thumb, not medical advice. Talk to a clinician before acting on them. Every source above is a link.
